quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
Try to hit only the side of the obstacle.
Speed up before hitting the obstacle.
Lean the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid riding over an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down, keep your motorcycle straight, rise slightly off your seat, and roll on the throttle just before contact.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Ride at a slower speed than usual.
Keep a shorter distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Ride at a faster speed than usual.
Brake a little later than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride at a slower speed than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. Your motorcycle will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing down earlier, increase your following distance, and look for bigger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not very harsh.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What can help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To avoid a crash, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid a sudden hazard.

questions.question: How can you prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride any motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, what should you NOT check?

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Yellow
Blue
Red
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When you turn a motorcycle, what happens to stopping traction?

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle is leaning to turn, some traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for stopping. You can brake while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus only on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but fail to notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help other drivers notice your motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your headlight on all the time, even during the day.
Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.
Use your horn every few minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time, even during the day.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times while riding. This helps other drivers notice your motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What is the best protection for motorcycle jackets and pants?

options.text: They should cover your arms and legs completely.
They should be loose and flap in the wind.
They should only partially cover your arms and legs.
They should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
The shaking makes it hard to use your mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering ability. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean with the operator as the motorcycle turns.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator as the motorcycle turns.
questions.explanation: Ask passengers to lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as comfortable without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for motorcycles?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves provide protection in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce your risk of a crash, stay alert and be ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which ones matter most. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding, what happens?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will not change.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:

options.text: Larger.
Farther away.
Faster.
Narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will fix itself.
Brake hard.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling—it will make it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean forward and down as much as you can, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Then find and fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothes.
Wear bright-colored clothes.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your crash risk, make yourself as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothes when riding, even during the day.
